latest_release.name: Mister Download Manager v0.5.2
latest_release.body:
**On a Mac?** The `-experimental` files are fresh builds for Mac (Apple Silicon and Intel) that we haven't tried ourselves yet. Want to be among the first? Give them a go and tell us how it went in an [issue](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues).

A big fixes release: YouTube and video downloads, crashes and freezes, downloads on slow disks, the Mac helper, plus a Safari extension, far more file types and a few new columns and options.

### Added

- **Torrent → Files…**: the list of a torrent's files for any torrent, running, stopped or finished, with a box to choose each (also a Files… button in File Properties).
- **Two columns for torrents in the download list** ([#357](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/357)): **Peers** (those a torrent has connected while it runs, seeders and leechers alike) and **Share ratio** (what it has sent against what it took), after **Transfer rate**. A layout saved before them gets them there.
- The extension's **Media on this page** can name a file after its page: **Prefix media file names with the page title** puts the page's title before the file's own name. Off as installed.
- **Far more file types taken from the browser by default** ([#382](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/382)): AI models and datasets (GGUF, SAFETENSORS, CKPT, PT, ONNX, PARQUET...), 3D and CAD (GLB, FBX, OBJ, STL, BLEND, STEP...), design and camera RAW files, ebooks, Office files, DAT, disk images and split archives. A list you never edited gains them; one you edited stays yours.
- **A Safari extension, inside the Mac app:** a click on a link to a file type MDM takes goes to MDM, and so do the right-click items, the button over videos and **Media on this page**, as in the other browsers. Safari gives extensions no access to its downloads, so a download a page starts by itself stays with Safari, and the browser's proxy is not shared. See [Browser integration](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/blob/v0.5.2/docs/browser-integration.md#safari-macos).
- Help: what to do when an antivirus or VirusTotal flags MDM, and how to check your copy is the real one.

### Changed

- In English, the **Last Try Date** and **Added** columns follow the system's 12- or 24-hour clock: `Oct 28 9:44:12 PM 2026` when Windows uses a 12-hour clock, and **Added** starts wide enough for it ([#392](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/392)).

### Fixed

- With no tray icon to come back from, closing or minimizing the main window now leaves it in the taskbar, with downloads still going, instead of hiding it with no way back. **Options → General → Keep running when closing the window** (on by default) makes closing quit MDM when unticked ([#457](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/pull/457)).
- Crash reports: a crash monitor that can't open its connection no longer makes MDM wait five seconds at start or stays behind as a second process ([#458](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/pull/458)).
- Download File Info no longer stays open but out of sight, with every later download waiting behind it ([#440](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/440)). The next one after answering **Create folder** came up as an invisible window, and on Windows one hidden with a minimized main window is now shown again, as is the duplicate question
- A file name sent by a site in plain UTF-8 now reaches MDM readable from Firefox and browsers built on it, such as Floorp, Waterfox and Zen: an Arabic name was saved as unreadable symbols ([#447](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/447)). A name written with percent signs in the same header is decoded as well. The add-on carries the fix
- A download saved under a numbered name because another file already had its name (`master (1).mp4`) now shows that name in the list and opens its own file, instead of keeping the old name and opening the other file ([#442](h

detail.readme:
# Mister Download Manager

Downloads faster than IDM. Free, forever.

🌐 misterdownloadmanager.com: the official website, with the downloads, help and news

🧩 Browser extension:

The Chrome Web Store's is for Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi and Helium too (how).


⭐ Like it? Give it a star. MDM has no ads and no marketing budget: stars are how people find it.

Windows 10 and 11 · Linux (Ubuntu, Debian, Mint, Fedora, openSUSE, Arch and more) · macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel, experimental)
86 languages · no ads, no trial, no sign-up

5×

Faster
a 1 GB file: 1 s instead of 5.5 s

+46

More languages
86 instead of IDM's 40

100%

Cheaper (free!)
no licence, no trial, ever

Torrent

Supported fully
magnet links, .torrent files, seeding

| 🚀 [Download](#download) | ⚡ [Why switch](#why-switch-from-idm) | 🖼️ [Screenshots](#screenshots) | ✨ [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md) | 📜 [Help and tutorials](docs/README.md) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ## Why switch from IDM? **Same window you know. Your downloads finish sooner. And it costs nothing.**

| | Mister Download Manager | IDM 6.42 | | --- | --- | --- | | Download a big file (1 GB) | **1 second** | 5.5 seconds | | Download a small file | **instantly** | 3.1 seconds | | Download over a shaky connection | **1.6 seconds** | 5.4 seconds | | Wait before a download starts | **instantly** | 3.1 seconds | | Price | **Free, forever** | Paid, after a 30-day trial | | Ads, nag screens, sign-up | **None** | Registration needed | | Open source | **Yes** (GPL) | No | Nothing new to learn: the toolbar, the categories, the list of downloads, the progress window and the browser button are where you expect them. Measured on the same computer, same files, both programs at their default settings ([how we measured](#the-benchmark-in-detail)). ## Download

On the [download page](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/releases/latest), pick one: | File | Choose it when | | --- | --- | | **`...-setup.exe`** | **Not sure? Take this one.** It installs MDM, connects it to your browser and asks your language. | | `...-portable.zip` | You want MDM on a USB stick or without installing: unzip and run. Everything stays in its folder. | | `...-x64.zip` | You want the plain programs without an installer. | | `...-extension-chromium.zip` | You want to add the browser extension by hand (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi). From the stores is easier: [Add to Chrome](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/mister-download-manager/ejoleppdfgjdndddcjoehopknmlglojp), [Add to Firefox](https://addons.mozilla.org/firefox/addon/mister-download-manager/). | > [!NOTE] > Windows may say *"Windows protected your PC"* the first time, because this early version isn't > code-signed yet. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. Or with [WinGet](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/package-manager/winget/), Windows' package manager: in a terminal, the first line installs MDM and the second updates it. ``` winget install AhmedNefzaoui.MisterDownloadManager winget upgrade AhmedNefzaoui.MisterDownloadManager ``` ### On Linux MDM runs on Linux too, tested on Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 12 and Fedora with GNOME, KDE Plasma, Xfce and Cinnamon, on X11 and in Wayland sessions: the tray, dark mode, browser integration (Ubuntu's Snap Firefox included) and the packages' installs. Not there yet: screen readers (Orca) don't read its windows, and Flatpak browsers can't reach it ([more](docs/getting-started.md#on-linux)). Up to version 0.2.4, the files' names end in `-experimental`. | File | For | | --- | --- | | `...-linux-x86_64.deb` | Ubuntu, Debian, Mint, Pop!_OS: `sudo apt install ./.deb`. | | `...-linux-x86_64.rpm` | Fedora, openSUSE, RHEL: `sudo dnf install ./.rpm`. | | `...-linux-x86_64.AppImage` | Any Linux. Make it executable and run it. | | `...-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | The plain programs, for any distribution. |

### On a Mac? Be the first to try it Fresh builds for **macOS** (Apple Silicon and Intel) are on the same download page, marked `-experimental`: we haven't tried them on a Mac ourselves yet. Give them a go and [tell us how it went](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/new/choose); you'll help make them as solid as the Windows and Linux versions. | File | For | | --- | --- | | `...-macos-arm64-experimental.dmg` | Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or later). Open it and drag MDM to Applications. The first time, right-click the app and choose **Open**. | | `...-macos-x86_64-experimental.dmg` | Mac with an Intel processor, the same way. | ## 🌍 In your language Every language Windows 11 offers, **86 in all**. MDM asks on its first start, and you can change it any time in **View → Language**. Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and Uyghur get a fully mirrored, right-to-left window.

## Screenshots

One click on YouTube: the Download video button appears over the video.
Any video on any page: drag the button where you like, it stays there.

Watch it fly: every connection's share of the file, live speed and time left.
Dark mode that follows Windows.

Add a download: paste a link, or let MDM catch it from your browser.
Torrents and magnet links: pick the files you want, skip the rest.

A torrent's progress: its files, peers, trackers and pieces, in tabs.
A video's progress: speed and time left while yt-dlp brings it in.

86 languages, chosen by flag on the first start.
Right to left for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and Uyghur.

Download overnight: queues that start and stop on their own.
Options where you expect them, every control working.
## What it does - **Speeds up every download** by fetching parts of the file at the same time, and keeps re-balancing until the last byte. - **Resumes** after a crash, a restart or a dropped connection, without starting over. - **Catches downloads from Firefox, Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi and Helium** (the extension is on Firefox Add-ons and the Chrome Web Store), and gives them back to the browser when MDM isn't running. - **Downloads videos** from web pages (a button appears over the video; playlists, subtitles, the sound alone), **image galleries** with gallery-dl, and **torrents and magnet links** (sequential order, RSS feeds, sharing limits). - **Many links at once**: the Link grabber sorts them into packages and extracts the archives (zip, 7z, rar) when they're in. Debrid accounts (Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, Premiumize, TorBox; experimental) download file-host links through your own account. - **Downloads overnight** with queues and a scheduler that can wake the computer, then shuts it down if you like. - **Through your VPN only**, if you want: hold every download to one network adapter, with a kill switch, and choose an encrypted DNS. Each download shows its server's country. - **From your phone, or on a server**: control MDM from a phone on your home network, or run it without a window on a NAS (Docker, Unraid) ([how](docs/server.md)). - **Works from scripts too**: IDM's command-line switches, a command-line tool, and a local API for other programs ([how](docs/command-line.md)). - **Works with your AI assistant**: an MCP server lets Claude, Cursor or VS Code list, add, pause and remove your downloads ([set it up](docs/ai-assistants.md)). - **Leaves you some speed**: limit one download or all of them, only while you're at the computer. - **Day and dark mode, and themes**: Classic, Native, High contrast, Metro, Adwaita, Breeze, Luna, Aero and Aqua, or your own in a text file ([how](docs/themes.md)). Everything larger, up to 200 %, with **View → Interface size**. 86 languages, and a portable version for USB sticks. - **Works from the keyboard and with screen readers** (Narrator, NVDA): every window, dialog and menu ([the keys](docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)). - **No ads, no trial, no account**. Free and open source. Step by step: [your first download](docs/guide-first-download.md) · [catch every browser download](docs/guide-catch-browser-downloads.md) · [download overnight](docs/guide-download-overnight.md) · [download a video](docs/guide-video-from-page.md) · [all help pages](docs/README.md) --- ## The benchmark in detail Both programs downloaded the same files from the same local test server ([labserver](crates/labserver)), with the network trouble each scenario names: seven runs each, both at their default settings. MDM finished first in **all seven scenarios**; every difference is statistically significant (Mann-Whitney p < 0.001), and MDM used less CPU in every one.

On a server that allows only two connections, MDM used 2 and still finished first; IDM opened 480. The full table, the machine and the raw data: [docs/bench/run5/REPORT.md](docs/bench/run5/REPORT.md). The harness is in [tools/bench](tools/bench), so anyone can run it again. ## Not a reverse-engineering project MDM is an independent, clean-room program. It is a new implementation of a familiar way of working, not a copy of anyone's software. - **No one else's code or assets.** It contains no code, binaries, artwork, icons, sounds or text from Internet Download Manager, nor code from any other download manager. The app icon was made for MDM with ChatGPT (OpenAI's image generation); the other icons come from openly licensed sets ([ATTRIBUTION.md](ATTRIBUTION.md)). - **Nothing taken apart.** No IDM file was ever disassembled, decompiled, debugged, patched or inspected below its user interface, and its licensing, trial and registration were never touched or bypassed. - **Learned as a user learns.** What MDM does was learned from IDM's public documentation and help pages, its public screenshots, and by using a licensed copy as a black box: downloading test files from our own test server ([labserver](crates/labserver)) and watching what reached the network and the screen. - **Built on public standards.** The download engine follows the HTTP specifications (RFC 9110, RFC 9112) and was designed, tested and measured independently. Its speed comes from its own design, which the benchmark shows. - **Not affiliated.** MDM isn't affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Tonec Inc. "Internet Download Manager" and "IDM" are trademarks of their owner, named here only to describe the layout people already know and to compare the two programs. ## For developers
Build from source Requires Rust stable 1.98 or later (the MSVC toolchain on Windows), and for the engine's browser-like connection (BoringSSL, built from source): CMake, LLVM's libclang and, on Windows, NASM (`winget install Kitware.CMake LLVM.LLVM NASM.NASM`; on Linux `cmake` and `libclang-dev`; on macOS Xcode's command line tools and `cmake`). `cargo build -p mdm-app --no-default-features` builds the app without it (a site that refuses MDM's own connection then stays refused). ``` cargo build --release cargo test ``` This makes `misterdownloadmanager.exe` (the app), `misterdownloadmanager-cli.exe` (headless command line), `misterdownloadmanager-mcp.exe` (the MCP server for AI assistants) and `misterdownloadmanager-nmhost.exe` (the browser host) in `target\release\`. `tools\installer\build.ps1` builds the installer and both zips into `target\dist\` (needs [Inno Setup 6](https://jrsoftware.org/isinfo.php)); a `vX.Y.Z` tag does the same on GitHub Actions and publishes the release. Browser integration from a build: register the native messaging host with `target\release\misterdownloadmanager-nmhost.exe --register` (undo with `--unregister`), then in `chrome://extensions` or `edge://extensions` turn on Developer mode, **Load unpacked** and pick the `extension/` folder (its ID is always `oogbclbbninliongijffeeggalppliok`).
Layout and tools A Cargo workspace (edition 2024); [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) explains how the pieces fit. | Crate | What it is | |---|---| | [`mdm-engine`](crates/engine) | The download engine: segmentation, connections, resume, limits | | [`mdm-app`](crates/app) | The desktop app (egui), and `--headless` for servers | | [`mdm-cli`](crates/cli) | Headless downloads from the command line | | [`mdm-mcp`](crates/mcp) | The MCP server, for AI assistants | | [`mdm-nmhost`](crates/nmhost) | The browser's native messaging host | | [`mdm-ipc`](crates/ipc) | Talking to a running app; shared capture rules; the extension's IDs | | [`mdm-remote`](crates/remote) | The remote control: the HTTPS server and page a paired phone uses | | [`mdm-crash`](crates/crash) | Crash and freeze reports: the monitor, minidumps, stacks | | [`mdm-debrid`](crates/debrid) | Debrid accounts through the services' official APIs | | [`mdm-extract`](crates/extract) | Archive extraction (zip, tar, gz, xz; 7z and RAR through 7-Zip) | | [`mdm-geo`](crates/geo) | A server's country, from an IP table on this computer | | [`mdm-tools`](crates/tools) | yt-dlp and ffmpeg for video pages, gallery-dl for galleries | | [`mdm-torrent`](crates/torrent) | BitTorrent through librqbit | | [`mdm-labserver`](crates/labserver) | An HTTP test server with fault injection, for tests and benchmarks | | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `tools\dev\check-cross.ps1` | Checks the code for Linux and macOS from Windows (with [Zig](https://ziglang.org) as the C compiler) | | `node tools/extension/e2e.mjs` | The browser extension in real Chrome, Brave, Edge and Firefox, headless: a link's download must reach MDM (or another MDM, a server); on Windows and Linux | | `python tools/i18n/extract.py` | Lists every interface text in `i18n/en.tsv` (CI checks it matches the code) | | `python tools/i18n/translate.py` | Translates what the catalogs lack (checks every row in code) | | `python tools/installer/languages.py` | The installer's messages in every language | | `node tools/readme/build.mjs` | This page's pictures, comparison table and flags, from the benchmark data | | `tools\lab\docs-shots.ps1` | The screenshots, from a separate test instance (`/show ` opens each window), off the screen | | `python tools/shots/make.py` | The help pages' pictures, from one list (`tools/shots/shots.toml`): shot, cropped, annotated, lossless WebP; `make.py check` keeps them in step | | `tools/lab/wsl/` | A WSL2 machine that builds MDM for Linux in minutes and shoots its windows on a virtual screen ([README](tools/lab/wsl/README.md)) | | `tools\lab\progress-shots.ps1` | The progress window of a video (yt-dlp) and of a torrent, from a swarm on this computer (`cargo run -p mdm-torrent --example swarm`) | | `python tools/website/build.py --serve` | misterdownloadmanager.com into `target/site` (help pages from `docs/`, news from the CHANGELOG, FAQ and legal pages from `website/content/`), served on http://127.0.0.1:8765; GitHub Pages publishes it (`pages.yml`) | | `python tools/readme/social.py` | The repository's social preview card (`docs/images/social-preview.png`) | | `MDM_FIT_AUDIT=` | Lists every text that doesn't fit its window or runs over another, for checking a translation | | `MDM_OFFSCREEN=1` | Opens every window off the screen, without focus, tray icon or sound (screenshots and checks) | | `MDM_TEST_TRASH_DIR=` | Tests only: archives deleted after extracting go into this folder, never into the real Recycle Bin or Trash | | `MDM_TEST_7ZIP=\|none` | Tests only: the 7-Zip program to use for 7z and RAR archives, or `none` to act as if 7-Zip weren't installed |
## Status and helping out MDM is young: the engine, the main window and the browser integration are solid on Windows and Linux, and some corners are still "good enough for now". - **Translations are machine-made.** Rows marked `#, machine` in [`i18n/`](i18n) wait for a native speaker; fixing one is a one-line pull request ([how](docs/languages.md)). Malay's menus, toolbar and download-list columns have been reviewed by a native speaker. - Not yet: code signing. The macOS builds are untested; on Linux, screen readers (Orca) and Flatpak browsers aren't supported yet. Bug reports are welcome in [Issues](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/new/choose): **Help → Report a problem** in the app fills in your version and system. Ideas are welcome in [Discussions](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/discussions/categories/ideas). Pull requests are accepted under the same licence: start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Made possible by these amazing humans Everyone who sent a pull request, opened an issue or joined a conversation here: thank you. People with pull requests first, then issues, then comments; [the website](https://misterdownloadmanager.com/contributors.html) shows what each one did.

## ⭐ Star history If MDM saves you time, a star is the quickest way to say so, and it helps the next person find a free download manager. [Star it on GitHub](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/stargazers). ## Support MDM MDM is free and always will be. If it saves you time, you can support its creator on [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/anefzaoui). It's optional: nothing in the app changes or unlocks, and there is no paid edition. ## Licence and credits Copyright (c) 2026 Ahmed Nefzaoui. Mister Download Manager is free software under the [GNU General Public License, version 3](LICENSE) or (at your option) any later version. Built on [egui](https://github.com/emilk/egui) through [storytold's forks](https://github.com/storytold/egui) and [storytold/craft-libs](https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs) (MIT OR Apache-2.0), [librqbit](https://github.com/ikatson/rqbit) (Apache-2.0), [zip](https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2) (MIT), and [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp) (Unlicense, run as a separate program; as are 7-Zip for 7z and RAR archives). Flags from [flag-icons](https://github.com/lipis/flag-icons) (MIT); pictures drawn with [rough.js](https://roughjs.com/) (MIT) in [Patrick Hand](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Patrick+Hand) (SIL OFL) and [Vega-Lite](https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/) (BSD-3). Bundled icons and artwork keep their own licences, listed in [ATTRIBUTION.md](ATTRIBUTION.md).
